scope: Independent incremental review of MCP retained-selection and draft-navigation CI repairs
method: Read the exact three-file diff against the failed candidate; followed McpPanel selection, displayedServers/lastServers, identity remount, allowed/start, accepted/recovered body and resource-read ownership boundaries; read usePaged fully, the changed MCP fixtures/cases and the complete navigation test.

usePaged removes its current-owner data while refreshing. The existing editor already retains lastServers in that interval; the select now shares that same display list. Disabled state includes loading, read error and snapshotKey mismatch, avoiding an absent option becoming an empty DOM selection.

The existing allowed/start guard still independently requires current discovery, connected and visible ownership, loaded thread, no pending/unknown operation, and appropriate confirmation/idle state; it is unchanged. Retained display does not authorize mutation.
McpPanel identity remount still separates api/epoch/runtimeEpoch/lease/thread/project/connection, so retained options are not newly reused across those ownership changes.

The accepted-body tests now wait until the selector is actually usable while the old body promise remains pending. They still start a newer read, resolve the old body, assert the newer read stays busy and assert no extra tool mutation.
The two new deferred refresh cases assert actual DOM option value and retained draft across pending and success/failure; these checks directly exercise the previously missing-option defect.

DraftsSettings renders the native identity prefix before project name. Updating the exact label to 普通 · Project B preserves all sole-draft, settings-open, fresh-discard-consent and eventual-navigation assertions.
limitations: This is an incremental repair review and an independent Windows/jsdom rerun of the two changed test files, not a new whole-web audit or physical browser acceptance.

The added delayed-refresh tests assert call-disabled state without establishing a confirmed call beforehand; the unchanged allowed/start guard was separately inspected, and the existing mutation tests were rerun. No stronger claim of a new adversarial handler-bypass test is made.
No source or test file was changed by this reviewer for the web review; no full-suite, paid inference, external MCP or deployment was performed.
The prior failed full CI remains failed; a successful targeted review does not satisfy the final coverage gate.
